sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

This application is filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita for regular bail in connection with F.I.R. No.11195003240067 of 2024 registered with Amirgadh Police Station,
District Banaskantha, for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 465, 468, 471 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2. Learned advocate for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has been arrested in connection with the present offence since 05.02.2024.

After earlier application filed by the present applicant having been withdrawn by the present applicant, the trial of the offence has commenced and upon consideration of the depositions of the witnesses on record so far, no case of any forgery having been done by the applicant is made out and in that event, the applicant is required to be NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/17882/2025 ORDER DATED: 04/09/2025 undefined prosecuted only in the offence of cheating which is punishable for imprisonment upto 7 years and the applicant has undergone substaintial period of incarceration.

It is alleged against the applicant that he had Kirankumar Babubhai Ranavasiya vs State Of Gujarat on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179590203/
1 forged certain documents.

sentences.text: However, what is produced on record before the learned trial Court is merely xerox copy of the said documents, which is not admissible any evidence.

He has further submitted that the co-accused, who has played more graver role than the present applicant has been considered for grant of bail and therefore, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail on the ground of parity.
He has, therefore, submitted that considering the nature of offence and role attributed to the applicant, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.
3. The learned APP appearing for the respondent State has vehemently submitted that the offences alleged against the present applicant is serious in nature.

He has further submitted that the allegations against the applicant, are serious in nature and looking to the facts as well as the allegations made against the applicant, no discretion should be exercised.

4. Heard learned advocates for the respective parties and perused the documents produced on record.
5.
At the outset, it is required to be noted that this a fourth successive application filed by the applicant in the present offence.
Earlier, the applicant had filed Criminal Misc. Application No.9102 of 2024 seeking regular bail, which was dismissed by this Court vide order dated 09.05.2024.

While NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/17882/2025 ORDER DATED: 04/09/2025 undefined dismissing the said application, this Court had made following observations in Paragraph Nos.4 and 5 :-
"4.
Heard learned advocates for the parties and perused the material available on record.
from the record, it appears that the present offence pertains to a scam of a sizable magnitude, wherein various parcels of land belonging to Government are involved.

The record indicates that the present applicant had approached various persons, who were illiterate and had assured them that he would get a parcel of land allotted to them and had collected huge amounts from those persons, and therefore,
had handed over them forged orders of Mamlatdar, Amirgadh allotting various parcels of land in their favour.
The present applicant was also found in possession of various rubber stamps in the name of Mamlatdar, Amirgadh.
It is believed that the present applicant had handed over such forged orders to at at least 50 persons and had collected huge amount from those illiterate persons.

5. So far as the aspect of parity is concerned, the other co-accused has been considered for grant of regular bail by this Court was an accomplice of the present applicant and the only role attributed to him was he had received the benefit of Rs.28,80,500/- whereas the role attributed to the present applicant is much more serious than the said co- accused and the applicant is the main perpetrator in the present offence.

6. After dismissal of the said application, the applicant had preferred another application being Criminal Misc. Application No.17424 of 2024, which was allowed to be withdrawn by this Court vide order dated 09.09.2024 since this NEUTRAL Kirankumar Babubhai Ranavasiya vs State Of Gujarat on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179590203/
2 CITATION R/CR.MA/17882/2025 ORDER DATED: 04/09/2025 undefined Court was not inclined to exercise its discretion in favour of the applicant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Learned advocate appearing for the applicant is not in position to show any change in circumstances after dismissal and withdrawal of the earlier application filed by the applicant.

It is sought to be contended on behalf of the applicant that the trial of the offence has commenced and depositions of several witnesses have been recorded and upon considering those depositions, offence of forgery is not made out against the present applicant.
8.
As submitted by learned advocate appearing for the applicant, the trial of the offence has commenced and few depositions have already been recorded.

The trial Court is yet to appreciate the evidence led before it and therefore, at this stage, it would not be appropriate for this Court to come to the conclusion that the offence of forgery is not made out against the present applicant.
It is also required to be noted that the prosecution has not yet led its evidence before the learned trial Court.

9. It is sought to be contended on behalf of the applicant that the other co-accused has been considered for grant of bail by this Court and this Court in its order dated 09.05.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Application No.9102 of 2024 had already taken this aspect into consideration.
10. Having regard to the aforesaid facts, this Court is not NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/17882/2025 ORDER DATED: 04/09/2025 undefined inclined to exercise its judicial discretion in favour of the applicant.
The application is dismissed.
